points.requirement: Separate purified binding, interaction in a relevant cellular system, biological-effect measurement and clinical benefit/harm evidence; a target name does not establish all four.

evidence.explanation: Current root text separates binding, relevant-system engagement and effect measurement.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Binding is an interaction between molecules and can be shown with a purified protein, which does not show that the compound reaches the protein inside a cell. Target engagement asks whether the interaction occurs in the relevant cells or tissue, and exposure, target location and the cell membrane all bear on it; a blood concentration and a concentration at an intracellular target are different observations. The cellular thermal shift assay of Martinez Molina and colleagues was developed to evaluate drug binding to target proteins in cells and tissue samples, and its authors used it to monitor drug transport and activation, off-target effects and resistance in cancer cell lines. Binding is also different from changing function: a compound can inhibit an enzyme, activate a receptor or deliver a payload, and a binder can leave the target's activity unchanged. Binding assays test an interaction under specified conditions and engagement assays examine the relevant cells or tissue, while a downstream signal measures a biological consequence and is not automatically a direct measure of how much of the target is occupied; growth, death and regrowth assays add further layers.

evidence.explanation: Clinical benefit and harm require their own setting-specific evidence.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The last step is clinical. Mechanistic plausibility does not show benefit, because the target may also be present in healthy tissue and the useful margin depends on achieved benefit and harm in a stated disease, treatment setting, product and outcome. The National Cancer Institute adds that cancer cells can become resistant to targeted therapy when the target itself changes so the drug can no longer interact with it, or when cells find new ways to grow that do not depend on the target.

points.requirement: The engagement question must require interaction, and schematic effect/clinical graphics must not imply a measured direction without a defined readout or study.
remaining: The assigned legacy PNG still asks whether the drug reaches the target rather than whether the relevant-system interaction is measured.
The legacy effect and clinical bar shapes have no defined axis/readout or named empirical study. Their own artwork convention remains an owner follow-up; v2 acceptance is not borrowed.
